structured_output.hypothesis: If hard-shelled eggs are prolate and never oblate spheroids, then essentially every measured bird egg has maximum length greater than maximum breadth, and no species has a mean length/breadth ratio below 1.
structured_output.pass_criterion: Using per-egg length (L) and maximum breadth (B), the claim is supported if (a) zero species in the dataset have a mean L/B < 1.00, and (b) fewer than 0.5% of individual eggs have L/B < 1.00, with all such eggs having L/B ≥ 0.95 (consistent with measurement error rather than a truly oblate shape).
structured_output.fail_criterion: The claim is refuted if any species (with at least 3 eggs) has a mean L/B < 0.97, or if 1% or more of individual eggs have L/B < 0.97, or if 3 or more species have mean L/B < 1.00 with most of their individual eggs below 1.
structured_output.interpretation: Thompson's 'prolate spheroid' is a solid of revolution whose axis of symmetry (egg length) is longer than its equatorial diameter (maximum breadth). 'Oblate' or 'flattened/discoidal' means the axis is shorter than the equatorial diameter. This is measured as the elongation ratio L/B (>1 prolate, <1 oblate, =1 spherical). Thompson himself notes that real eggs are asymmetric (ovoid, pointed at one end), so the test checks only the prolate-versus-oblate dimension criterion, not exact spheroidal geometry. The claim concerns hard-shelled eggs in general, but this dataset covers birds only (955 species), so reptile and other eggs are outside the test. Length and breadth are assumed to be maximum length and maximum breadth in mm. Exact column names must be confirmed from the dataset's README.txt before analysis.

dataset.name: Data from: The evolution of egg shape in birds: Evolutionary constraints and adaptations
dataset.publisher: Dryad (data authors: Robert Montgomerie, Tim Birkhead, James Thompson, Nicola Hemmings)
dataset.why_it_fits: Eggs from 955 bird species across 39 of 40 orders. Files include DATAraweggs.csv (individual egg measurements) and DATAeggshape.csv (per-species egg shape data). Fields to use (confirm names in README.txt): egg length, maximum breadth, species identifier. L/B is computed per egg and as a per-species mean.
